title: Went to bed last night with just the basics of a level-generator, woke up to a parametrized, multi-biome harness with decent test sheets.
author: HaMMeReD
selftext:
Building a breakout style game on top of Custom rust CA/SDF Engine (I.e. Falling Sand Sims, Metaballs). The goal is to have a upper screen "arena" with generative worlds, with diverse materials and biomes, and space in the bottom for the paddle/play area.

The second image is what the contact sheet looked like before bed (\~T150). The 3rd image is AI generated "north-star" visions to give the AI kind of a goal to work towards. It's not expected to reach this 1:1 because the engine is not made to draw like this. It's more for the guidance/grounding aspect. I'd regenerate this every once an a while based on the output of the harness so it'd stay somewhat grounded.

Wasn't completely automated. Did 220 iterations of the loop that analyzes screenshots, reads design docs and makes plans to improve, test the improvements and commit/reject each step of the way. Paused about every \~50 for a retrospective and to adjust the harness and run a few manual prompts.  
  
I had to pause \~50 iterations and do an eval/retro of progress. It wasn't all clear sailing, 0-50, didn't build the tooling right, was doing CPU eval instead of GPU eval leading to bad evals.

Stopped to fix the CPU vs GPU eval (and tear down CPU options in the first place)

50-100: Was on GPU eval, but was over-authoring. Extended the design language to allow lines/circles/squares and was placing them, which is not what I wanted. 

Stopped to fix the hard-coded authoring tools and remove them, and put safeguards so they don't return.

100-150: Authoring was mostly torn down, but wasn't making much progress because of overly complex level design.

Stopped to re-evaluate the generated level and get it from \~2000+ instructions to 300. (Levels are generated by a Rust DSL that generates a Graph, that compiles to Microcode that executes on GPU).  Also to refactor the design language and couplings so that the agent had more freedom to iterate without getting stuck.  I.e. in the OG templates it referred to materials directly, i.e. basalt, coal, sand. But I added theme indirection i.e. ROCK\_0 = Basalt, ROCK\_10 = Coal. That way it could theme the generation and not be semantically locked to the material.

150-220: Made really fast progress this time. The agent had freedom to iterate, wasn't design itself into a hole. It added a ton of biomes, really refined the test harness and the outputs. The loop also does retrospectives and updates itself as it goes.

Cost wise, probably cost me \~50% of my $200 codex plan weekly quota across 3 days. I'll definitely be setting up more agentic loop-style prompts that I can run, evaluate and iterate on in the future. Probably could have gone farther if I did each prompt but I doubt I'd even hit my quota if I did that, but this let me just leave it on auto-pilot for 8 hour stretches just glancing at it and intervening when it wasn't trending right.

comments.body:
If you could get very high resolutions these would make really cool worlds for a side-scroller.

How does the agent compare the quality of the images?

replies.author: HaMMeReD
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/1zn0ro82gc7h1.png?width=3811&format=png&auto=webp&s=65528ced0c3494dcff560f46a660f6bc1f27bd17

The engine does support tiles and large worlds. It's just the game that I'm working on first is scoped down a bit to a 512x512 board.

The generated biomes I have here are actually a bit more mature, overall I did them a while ago. The new ones are confined, and more actual game-focused and not just sandbox focused.

The scope down was kind of because I'm happy with where the engine is sitting but want to make a game, but don't want to over-reach.
